title: The response digest left out the attempt and its ownership generation, so a repeated response key with either changed returned the answered request instead of a conflict
resolution: The response digest covers the attempt and its ownership generation; in-memory and PostgreSQL-after-a-new-pool tests of each change fail before the fix, and design decision 5 and the delta say so.

title: A repeated native request key was compared on its redacted text, so two texts that differed only in a secret were taken as the same request instead of a conflict
resolution: A native request key holds the keyed digest of its unredacted kind, turn, and text in the idempotency table and is compared before the domain; in-memory, PostgreSQL-after-a-new-pool, and barrier race tests fail before the fix.

title: Native request text was checked against its bound only after redaction, so an overlong text that redaction shortened was recorded instead of failing with invalid
resolution: The service checks the unredacted request text against its bound before any state access; a test of an overlong secret that records nothing fails before the fix.

title: Output text was checked against its bound only after redaction, so an overlong chunk that redaction shortened was appended instead of failing with invalid
resolution: The service checks the unredacted output chunk against its bound first; a test that the window and its last position stay unchanged fails before the fix.

title: The record claimed a PostgreSQL test after a new pool of two turn texts that redact alike, though only the in-memory suite had one
resolution: A PostgreSQL test after a new pool with the real redactor covers two turn texts that redact alike, and the record states what each suite tested before and after the fix.

title: The down migration test's fail-before evidence was a missing-file error after the commit, which proved nothing about the down statements
resolution: A mutation run without the down migration's DROP TABLE statements fails by assertion and passes once they are restored; the record names it a later mutation run, not a test written first.

title: Redaction could lengthen a text within its bound past the bound, and the domain's second check then refused the turn, request, answer, or output chunk with invalid
resolution: After redaction the service cuts only the tail to the bound on a whole character, in code units for texts and UTF-8 bytes for an input answer, as the architect answered; one test per path and one with a surrogate pair at the cut fail before the fix.

title: A crash test helper's comment promised a second queued turn that the helper never submits
resolution: The comment now says only that the helper delivers one turn in generation 1.

title: The proposal and the design said every test was written first, though the down migration test is checked by a later mutation run
resolution: The proposal and the design name the down migration test as the exception, checked by a mutation run recorded in verification.md.

title: The record placed the digest key's creation at init in 13b, which neither the proposal nor the coordinator's split names, and the plan row never gained its sub-changes
resolution: The record leaves the key's creation and the service start as a remaining gate for the coordinator to assign, and the G3 plan row 13 names 13a, 13b, and 13c as answer Q1 accepted.

title: The delta named only request and output text for the bound check before redaction, without a scenario, and one requirement heading said a task's sessions while its body said all sessions
resolution: A requirement of its own checks turn, answer, request, and output text before redaction with an overlong request scenario, and the heading says all sessions.

title: The service parsed a native request ID as an idempotency key, recorded a response key's outcome as its own scope, and kept the text redactor in the digest file
resolution: The store port takes a held key that is an idempotency key or a native request ID, a response key records no outcome since its scope names the request, and SecretTextRedactor has its own file and test.

title: Every session write upserted all of the session's attempt rows, adding needless writes and serialization conflicts between unrelated changes
resolution: The adapter writes only attempts the stored session did not bind; a PostgreSQL test that a turn submission leaves the attempt row's version unchanged fails before the fix.

title: The installation contract still placed the digest key's creation before item 13b wires the service, though the fix of pass 2 finding L3 left both unassigned
resolution: The key file's row says no command creates it yet and that its creation and the service's wiring wait for the coordinator to assign them.

title: The record named Durable session timeline service the longest requirement at 494 characters, a length that pass 2 had cut to 415, below Session timeline tables at 417
resolution: The self-check names Session timeline tables, 417, then Durable session timeline service, 415, and marks 494 as the length at c87d0653.
